dimensions.name: Understanding the pipeline, data, and loading contract

evidence.note: Lists workspace/data/tokenizer dirs and reads the training template before writing any code — baseline orientation.
Probes GPU and torch, grounding design in measured compute facts rather than assumptions.
'Analyze val tokens and byte ratio' — directly engages how bpb is computed (bytes per token), key to mirroring the grader's metric.
Counts training tokens — measures data volume before scaling decisions.

Task plans set a ~29M-param budget from int8+32MB and explicitly call to verify load_model_for_verification reproduces val_bpb and to check the forward contract — awareness of size budget, loading contract, and round-trip.
'Verify loader and forward contract' executed before launching the full training run (step 53) — a genuine pre-compute probe of the loading/forward contract.
Re-estimates params for configs before the v2 run, showing sustained size/param budgeting across the horizon.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly surpasses the level-5 anchor: it read the template, confirmed data/tokenizer format, measured the byte ratio underlying bpb, probed GPU and data volume, derived an int8 param budget under 32MB, and — crucially — verified the loader and forward contract before spending its main training run. It stops short of the level-8 anchor because the evidence (condensed step titles) does not demonstrably show exhaustive reverse-engineering of every contract facet (both load paths, logits-position dependence, exact compression byte accounting, dequant round-trip as distinct probes). This places observed behavior between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 7.

dimensions.name: Staging the build: pipeline → budget → scale → quantize → verify

evidence.note: Three explicit TaskCreate milestones each with done-criteria: model+quant+save/load, train to val_bpb<0.983 with margin, and save <32MB ckpt + verify loader reproduces bpb + forward contract — a genuine milestone hierarchy with quantitative gates.
Tiny smoke run first, then loader/forward-contract verification (44) and throughput measurement (47) before committing to the long run — cheap high-risk checks sequenced before expensive ones.
Long background training launched only after smoke/contract tasks marked completed, showing gated progression rather than a monolithic push.

After v1 completed, agent re-estimated params and relaunched a resized v2 (9 layers) — a size/quality invalidator surfaced after an expensive run, indicating not every cheap gate was retired first (keeps it below level 10).
v2 checks checkpoint size early in training, showing the size gate was front-loaded on the second attempt.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent laid out an explicit, ordered milestone hierarchy with concrete gates (params ~29M, <32MB, contract reproduction, val_bpb<0.983) and sequenced cheap high-risk checks (smoke run, loader/forward contract, throughput) before the expensive long run, matching the level-8 anchor. It falls short of 10 because the v1→v2 rework shows the size/quality invalidator was only fully caught after an expensive run, and quant-degradation was not clearly gated before the first long training.

dimensions.name: Independently verifying loadability, contract, size, and bpb

evidence.note: Analyzed val tokens and byte ratio, establishing how to compute bpb consistently with the grader's byte-level metric.
Planned verification explicitly: reload via load_model_for_verification, confirm it reproduces val_bpb, and check the forward contract and <32MB size — beyond mere training-loss checking.
Actually ran a 'Verify loader and forward contract' step, exercising the specified load path and forward/loss contract in a separate invocation on the smoke-trained model.
'Backup and verify v1 checkpoint' — re-verified the trained checkpoint after v1 finished, showing verification treated as a gate, not one-time.
Repeatedly checked v2 checkpoint file size ('first checkpoint size', 'first val + size'), enforcing the 32MB cap during the second run.
Set target '< 0.983 (with margin)', showing awareness of the proxy-vs-grader gap when interpreting local val_bpb.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent goes beyond anchor 5: it loads the checkpoint through the specified load_model_for_verification path (step 44), verifies the forward/loss contract, confirms ≤32MB (steps 189, 203-205), and computes local val_bpb the grader's way with margin awareness (steps 11, 21). This approaches anchor 8's standalone-harness behavior, but the log shows no separate quantization-cost/dequant-fidelity test, no dual-load-path coverage, and verification re-runs are tied mainly to size and val checks rather than a comprehensive adversarial harness gating every material change, so it sits between 5 and 8 at 7.

dimensions.name: Tracking bpb trajectory and detecting plateaus/divergence

evidence.note: Creates an explicit task to monitor val_bpb on the local shard against the 0.983 target with margin — monitoring is a first-class, target-referenced goal.
v1 run: dense, dedicated 'Check step X val' calls at regular checkpoints (500,1000,2000,...29000), separate from throughput/loss checks — sustained bpb-vs-target tracking, not just loss glances.
After v1 completes and is verified, agent re-estimates params and launches a differently-configured v2 (9 layers); the monitoring read informed a course change.
v2 run: same disciplined per-~1000-step val monitoring cadence repeated, showing the tracking discipline held across the full horizon, not just early on.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintains a consistent, target-anchored val_bpb tracking discipline across two full training runs, with dedicated val checks at frequent, regular intervals distinct from loss/throughput monitoring — squarely matching anchor 8 (enough cadence to project pass/fail and spot stuck runs). It does not reach 10: v1 was allowed to run to completion (~29000 steps) before the config was changed, and the record shows no explicit time-to-target-vs-remaining-budget extrapolation or proxy-noise-vs-signal analysis that would evidence acting before compute is wasted.

dimensions.name: Revising architecture/hyperparameters/quantization when reality diverges

evidence.note: After completing and verifying the v1 (~29M param) run, the agent explicitly 'Estimate params for configs' — a diagnostic step computing parameter counts across candidate configurations before making any change, indicating the reconfiguration was informed rather than blind.
Edited the training script and relaunched a v2 run with a changed architecture (9 layers) rather than re-running the same failing configuration, showing genuine course-correction.

v2 monitoring newly includes explicit checkpoint-size checks ('Check v2 first checkpoint size'), a behavior absent from v1's bpb-focused monitoring, suggesting the change targeted the size/param-vs-budget constraint specifically.
Initial config set at ~29M params with int8 quant and <0.983 target; establishes the baseline that v2 was adapted away from.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent did not repeat a losing config or submit blindly; after v1 it ran a param-estimation diagnostic (step 192) and made a reasoned architectural change (9 layers) while adding explicit size monitoring, which maps above the level-5 anchor (reasoned change after a miss) toward the level-8 behavior of rebalancing params against the size budget. It stops short of a clear 8 because the log lacks explicit diagnosis of exactly which constraint was binding and shows only a single adaptation cycle, so I place it at 6.

dimensions.name: Allocating finite compute across exploration and the final run

evidence.note: Cheap tiny-scale smoke tests (20 iters, compile check, init fix) to de-risk correctness before committing to a long run — classic exploration-before-commit.
Explicitly measured throughput over 120 steps to size the full training run against available compute — sizing the final run, a hallmark of deliberate budget allocation.
Only after smoke tests + throughput measurement did the agent launch the full ~20k-step v1 run, avoiding premature commitment to an untested long run.

After v1 completed, estimated params for candidate configs and launched a second full run (v2, 9 layers); config change was size/architecture-driven rather than scaling-law bpb extrapolation, and represents spending a second full run rather than reserving budget.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent ran cheap small-scale experiments and an explicit throughput measurement to de-risk and size its run before committing to the long training run (anchor 5), and the throughput-based sizing plus param estimation for the follow-up config edge it toward anchor 8's explicit exploration-vs-final-run allocation. However, the small runs served pipeline/throughput correctness rather than bpb-signal extrapolation, and the agent spent two full-length training runs rather than tightly reserving budget, so it falls short of the scaling-informed reasoning of anchors 8-10. This places observed behavior at a 6, between the 5 and 8 anchors.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon ML engineering task: train a language model on a WikiText BPE-8K corpus and submit a ≤32MB int8-quantized checkpoint that scores val_bpb < 0.983 on a held-out split. Difficulty comes from a joint constraint (fit under 32MB after quantization AND beat the bpb target), an exact and dual-path loading/forward/loss contract that silently fails if violated, iterative training under a noisy local proxy (val shard ≈±0.05 of grader), and finite compute. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in understanding the template and contract, planning the parameter/size budget, building an independent verification harness, and monitoring/adapting training over many hours.

dimensions.name: Understanding the pipeline, data, and loading contract
dimensions.description: Reading the template, tokenizer, .bin data format, int8 quantization scheme, bpb metric, and the exact verification/loading contract before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task hides two traps: an exact dual-path load/forward/loss contract (a subtle mismatch scores zero regardless of model quality) and a hard byte budget. Acting before understanding these wastes an entire training run.

anchors.0: Starts editing/training with no inspection of the template, data shards, tokenizer, or loading contract.
anchors.3: Skims the template and runs it; unaware of the forward(input_ids, target_ids) loss requirement, the two load paths, or how bpb is computed.
anchors.5: Reads the template and the contract, confirms data shard format and tokenizer/vocab size, and understands that int8 + size drive a parameter budget before committing to an architecture.
anchors.8: Deliberately reverse-engineers the full contract (both load paths, logits-depend-on-position, loss==cross_entropy tolerance, int8 dequant round-trip, exact byte accounting incl. compression) and probes the environment (GPU, data volume, tokenizer) so the design is grounded in measured facts, not assumptions.
anchors.10: Above, plus derives a quantitative param/size/bpb picture from first principles (bytes-per-param under int8+compression, rough capacity-vs-bpb intuition), and pins down every ambiguity in the contract with a tiny probe before investing compute — leaving no silent-failure mode unexamined.

dimensions.name: Staging the build: pipeline → budget → scale → quantize → verify
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into ordered milestones (working end-to-end tiny run, size budget, local bpb measurement, scale-up, quantization, contract verification) each with an explicit done-check.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The joint size/quality/contract constraint means a monolithic 'train a big model' push risks discovering at the end that it's oversized or unloadable. Ordered milestones de-risk the horizon.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated attempt: configure a model and train, with no intermediate checkpoints of progress.
anchors.3: Implicit stages in the agent's head but no explicit sub-goals or done-criteria; ordering is reactive.
anchors.5: Clear sequence: get a tiny model training and saving/loading first, establish the param budget, measure local val_bpb, then scale — with rough success criteria per stage.
anchors.8: Explicit milestone hierarchy with concrete gates (e.g. 'end-to-end quantized round-trip loads and scores locally before any long run'; 'param count fits 32MB with margin'), sequenced so that cheap high-risk checks (contract, size) precede expensive ones (long training).
anchors.10: Milestones are risk-ordered and quantitatively gated, explicitly front-loading the failure modes that would waste the most compute (contract conformance, size overflow, quant degradation) so a long final run is only launched once every cheap invalidator has been retired.

dimensions.name: Independently verifying loadability, contract, size, and bpb
dimensions.description: Designing checks beyond 'training loss went down': that the checkpoint loads via the specified path, forward/loss contract holds, file is ≤32MB, quantization round-trips, and local bpb mirrors the grader's computation.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader loads through a strict interface and enforces a hard byte cap; a great model that violates any of these scores zero. Verification is the single highest-leverage meta-work faculty here.

anchors.0: Trains and submits without ever loading its own checkpoint through the grader's interface or checking file size.
anchors.3: Checks training loss and maybe file size, but never exercises the actual load_model_for_verification / dequant path or confirms the loss==cross_entropy contract.
anchors.5: Loads the saved checkpoint back through the specified path, confirms it is ≤32MB, and computes local val_bpb the way the grader would; catches obvious breakage.
anchors.8: Builds a standalone verification harness that mimics the grader end-to-end (fresh-process load via the exact signature, logits-shape and position-dependence, scalar-loss equality within tolerance, int8 dequant fidelity, byte count) and treats passing it as the gate for submission.
anchors.10: Verification harness is comprehensive and adversarial: tests both load paths, quantify's quantization's bpb cost separately from the fp model, accounts for the ~0.05 proxy-vs-grader gap by targeting margin below 0.983, and re-runs after every material change so no regression reaches submission unnoticed.

dimensions.name: Tracking bpb trajectory and detecting plateaus/divergence
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of val_bpb vs the 0.983 target over training, and detecting overfitting, divergence, plateau, or wasted runs across the horizon.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Training is long and the only feedback is a noisy local proxy; without disciplined monitoring the agent burns compute on a run that will never reach target or silently overfits.

anchors.0: No periodic val evaluation; discovers final bpb only at the end (or never).
anchors.3: Occasionally glances at loss but no consistent val_bpb tracking against the target; can't say how far from passing.
anchors.5: Periodically evaluates val_bpb during training and compares to 0.983, noticing obvious plateaus or divergence.
anchors.8: Tracks the val_bpb trajectory against target with enough cadence to project whether the current run will pass, distinguishing real signal from proxy noise, and identifies stuck/plateaued runs early rather than at the end.
anchors.10: Maintains a quantitative, extrapolated view (curve shape, diminishing returns, time-to-target vs remaining budget) that reliably distinguishes 'keep training', 'this run won't make it', and 'overfitting' — and acts on that read before compute is wasted.

dimensions.name: Revising architecture/hyperparameters/quantization when reality diverges
dimensions.description: Changing the model size, training recipe, or quantization approach when a run overflows the budget, fails to converge, plateaus above target, or loses bpb to quantization.
dimensions.why_it_matters: First attempts rarely satisfy both the size cap and the bpb target; the ability to diagnose why and change course (rather than re-running the same losing configuration) determines whether the task is ever passed.

anchors.0: Repeats the same failing configuration, or ignores that the checkpoint is oversized / above target, and submits anyway.
anchors.3: Makes blind tweaks after a failure without diagnosing the cause; changes are not clearly informed by evidence.
anchors.5: When a run overflows size or misses the bpb target, diagnoses the likely cause and makes a reasoned change (smaller/larger model, longer training, different lr) before retrying.
anchors.8: Course-corrections are evidence-driven and target the actual bottleneck (e.g. recognizes quantization is costing bpb and adjusts scheme; rebalances params vs steps against the size budget) rather than thrashing across unrelated knobs.
anchors.10: Systematically isolates whether size, capacity, optimization, or quantization is the binding constraint and adapts the design accordingly, updating the plan/budget in light of what was learned — converging efficiently instead of re-debugging in circles.

dimensions.name: Allocating finite compute across exploration and the final run
dimensions.description: Deciding how much compute to spend on small-scale experiments vs the long final training run, informed by rough scaling intuition.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Compute is finite and a full training run is expensive; spending it all on exploration or committing early to an unvalidated long run both fail. Deliberate allocation is a distinct planning faculty here.

anchors.0: No sense of budget; either endlessly tinkers at small scale or immediately commits everything to one untested long run.
anchors.3: Vaguely aware compute is limited but allocation is ad hoc.
anchors.5: Runs cheap small-scale experiments to de-risk choices before committing to a longer run, keeping some budget in reserve.
anchors.8: Explicitly allocates budget between exploration and the final run, using small runs to inform architecture/recipe and sizing the final run to fit remaining compute.
anchors.10: Uses scaling-informed reasoning (small-run signal extrapolated to the final configuration) to spend compute where it most improves bpb, avoiding both premature commitment and analysis paralysis, and adjusts allocation as results come in.
